title: Reading Big-Endian and Little-Endian Multi-Byte Values
description:
Reading multi-byte integers byte-by-byte using shifts is portable, safe against unaligned memory access traps (which cause CPU HardFaults on Cortex-M0/M3), and independent of host endianness.

### Tasks:
1. `read_be16(buf)`: `(buf[0] << 8) | buf[1]`
2. `read_be32(buf)`: `(buf[0] << 24) | (buf[1] << 16) | (buf[2] << 8) | buf[3]`
3. `read_le16(buf)`: `(buf[1] << 8) | buf[0]`
4. `read_le32(buf)`: `(buf[3] << 24) | (buf[2] << 16) | (buf[1] << 8) | buf[0]`
hint: Never cast an unaligned byte pointer directly: `*(uint32_t*)buf` can crash the MCU with an alignment fault on unaligned addresses.
